documents.title: Academic Honesty Policy
documents.summary: The college-wide Student Handbook lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' as an academic honesty violation, its only AI wording. The rest of the page is the general hearing, evidence, sanction and appeal procedure.
documents.stance_why: The only AI text is 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence', named as an example of misrepresenting others' ideas or language as one's own; AI is thus banned unless approved, which is restrict.

units.why: The handbook lists 'unapproved use of artificial intelligence' among examples of representing others' ideas or language as one's own, so unapproved AI use is a named integrity violation for independently prepared work; it is addressed to students, sets a standard (general phase), and is a ban absent approval, so must-not/restrict; P36 fits because it classifies AI use as academic dishonesty (P01 is not chosen because the clause is framed as an integrity violation, not a course default).
units.anchor: unapproved use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: In projects and assignments (including homework)

units.why: Faculty who believe a student violated the standards 'must submit a complaint directly' to the Vice-President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students; this routes suspected violations, including the AI clause, into the integrity process, so it is an instructor duty in the misuse phase under P36.
units.anchor: they must submit a complaint directly to the Vice-President of Student Affairs/Dean of Students
units.frag_start: When a faculty member believes that
units.fit_note: General academic-honesty reporting procedure; AI is not mentioned in this sentence.

units.why: The Academic Discipline Board 'uses a clear and convincing standard' and defines it as evidence 'highly and substantially more probable to be true rather than untrue'; this sets the evidentiary bar for any finding including the AI clause, so P69 (standard of proof).

units.frag_end: rather than untrue.” (Cornell University Legal Information Initiative)
units.fit_note: General standard for all academic honesty violations; AI is not named.

units.why: The student 'must submit a written statement of their version of events' and evidence within three academic days, so accused students have a procedural right to present their side; this is P64 (respond to allegations), addressed to the student in the misuse phase.
units.anchor: submit a written statement of their version of events
units.frag_start: Within three (3) academic days of the charge
units.fit_note: Generic hearing procedure for all honesty charges; AI not named.

units.why: The handbook lists sanctions 'that may be imposed' from a lower grade on an assignment to an F in the course, suspension, loss of honors and expulsion; stating penalties in advance is P37 and applies to violations of the AI clause as well.

units.policy: Sanctions for academic honesty violations include a lower grade on an assignment, loss of credit on an assignment, an F on an assignment, an F in the course, make-up or additional work, suspension, loss of College honors, and expulsion.
units.fit_note: General sanctions list for all honesty violations; AI not named.

units.why: From Fall 2026 violations and sanctions become reportable to employers and graduate schools for 3 years after graduation; this is a consequence rule about records not covered by any listed type (not a penalty on the work itself), so UNCOVERED.

documents.summary: The CS department defines four tiers of AI use, from none to completely open, that each course must follow, piloted in Fall 2026. Each course picks its tier, and use outside the tier is an honor-policy violation.
